text: The hotel’s boarded windows and locked entrance made it seem [welcoming|unwelcoming|The boarded windows and locked entrance make “unwelcoming” the clear description.] from the road. A [luminously|luminous|Use the adjective before the noun “sign”.] sign still glowed above the entrance, but its light did little to soften the building’s [oppressively|oppressive|Use an adjective before the noun “silence”.] silence. Mara stepped inside [hesitant|hesitantly|Use an adverb to describe how Mara stepped.] and noticed that the wallpaper had begun to peel.

title: The museum label
text: The label described the sculpture as “ordinary”, yet its surface was [intricately|intricate|After “was”, use an adjective.] enough to reward a closer look. Thin lines [crosses|crossed|Use the past tense and plural subject “lines”.] the stone, forming a pattern that resembled a map. The guide spoke [dismissive|dismissively|Use an adverb to describe how the guide spoke.] about the artist’s early work, although several visitors found it [compellingly|compelling|After “found it”, use an adjective.] and asked to see more.

title: The final performance
text: The hall fell silent as the dancer entered. Her movements were [precisely|precise|After “were”, an adjective is needed.] despite the narrow stage. She did not rush; instead, she [gradual|gradually|Use an adverb to describe how she built the movement.] increased the pace until the music seemed to pulse around her. The ending was [unexpectedly|unexpected|After “was”, use an adjective.] but not confusing. Several audience members [rised|rose|The past tense of “rise” is “rose”.] to applaud.

title: A message in the snow
text: By morning, the footprints had almost disappeared beneath a fresh layer of snow. The caretaker studied the [faintly|faint|Use an adjective before the noun “marks”.] marks near the gate, which suggested that someone had left in a hurry. He [careful|carefully|Use “carefully” to describe how he examined them.] compared their size with the prints by the shed. The path was [desert|deserted|Use the adjective “deserted” after “was”.], but a bright scarf slid [silent|silently|Use an adverb to describe how the scarf slid.] beside the wall.

title: The changing shoreline
text: The town’s beach changed noticeably between 2015 and 2025. After each storm, the sea [erode|eroded|Use the past tense to match the completed period.] a little more of the sandy edge. New rocks made the coast appear [ruggedly|rugged|After “appear”, use an adjective.] and less inviting to swimmers. Local residents [argue|argued|Use the past tense to match the reported meeting.] about whether a barrier would help, while the council [careful|carefully|Use an adverb to describe how the council studied the plans.] examined several proposals.

title: The portrait in the corridor
text: At first glance, the portrait seemed [serenely|serene|After “seemed”, use an adjective to describe the subject.] and almost cheerful. Yet the artist had placed the figure beside a corner that remained [shadow|shadowy|After “remained”, use an adjective to describe the corner.], and its hands were tightly closed. The guide did not state the sitter’s feelings directly; instead, he [announced|insinuated|The guide hints at the sitter’s worry rather than stating it directly, so “insinuated” fits.] that the sitter had been anxious. A visitor appeared [skeptically|skeptical|Use an adjective after “appeared” to describe the visitor’s state.] and asked what evidence supported that reading.

title: A difficult apology
text: The apology sounded [sincerely|sincere|After “sounded”, use an adjective to describe the apology.] at first, but its careful wording avoided naming the harm. The speaker [repeated|repeatedly|Use an adverb to describe how often the speaker returned to the point.] praised the team’s patience while offering no plan to repair the damage. One listener was [unconvincingly|unconvinced|Use “unconvinced” to describe the listener’s response to the promise.] by the promise because its wording was vague. title: The flooded street
text: Residents moved quickly as water began to cover the lower road. A [steadily|steady|Use the adjective “steady” before the noun “current”.] current pushed leaves and small branches towards the drain. By evening, the rain had [intensify|intensified|Use the past participle after “had”.], and the street was closed.

title: The empty theatre
text: The theatre had once been lively, but now its seats were covered with dust. A [faintly|faint|Use an adjective before the noun “smell”.] smell of wood polish lingered near the stage, and a single lamp cast an [eerily|eerie|Use an adjective before the noun “glow”.] glow over the curtain. The caretaker [recall|recalled|Use the past tense to match the story.] the last performance with surprising detail. His voice grew [more quieter|quieter|Do not use “more” with the comparative “quieter”.] as he described the final applause.

title: The mountain photograph
text: The photograph looked [dramatic|dramatically|Use an adverb to modify “different”.] different when printed in black and white. Without colour, the pale sky seemed [vastly|vast|After “seemed”, use an adjective.] and the ridge appeared closer. The photographer [deliberate|deliberately|Use an adverb to describe how the photographer placed the figure.] placed a tiny figure near the lower edge. This choice [emphasise|emphasises|With the singular subject “choice”, use “emphasises”.] the scale of the landscape, while the dark foreground draws the viewer’s eye towards the peak.

title: The renovated library
text: The renovated library was designed to feel open, although its bare stone walls offered an [austerely|austere|Use an adjective to describe the noun “backdrop”.] backdrop. A faint scent of cedar [permeate|permeated|Use the past tense to match the completed renovation.] the reading room, while the furniture was arranged with [meticulously|meticulous|Use an adjective to describe the noun “care”.] care. The architect’s notes [stated|implied|The notes hinted at the aim without saying it directly, so “implied” is the precise verb.] that quiet work mattered more than display.

title: The ambiguous letter
text: The letter’s tone was deliberately [equivocal|equivocally|Use the adverb to modify “phrased”.] phrased, allowing its author to deny any firm promise. One sentence was [unequivocal|unequivocally|Use the adverb “unequivocally” before the adjective “clear”.] clear at first, but the next qualified it. Readers [infered|inferred|Double the “r” in the past tense “inferred”.] different intentions from the same wording. The final paragraph was so [laconicly|laconically|The adverb is spelled “laconically”.] concise that even close friends disagreed about what had been offered.

title: The old photograph
text: The photograph showed a jubilant crowd, yet the lone figure at its edge seemed [impassively|impassive|After “seemed”, use an adjective to describe the figure.] amid the celebration. This contrast [exacerbate|exacerbated|Use the past tense to match the description of the image.] the sense of isolation. A caption [ostensible|ostensibly|Use the adverb “ostensibly” to modify “claimed”.] claimed that everyone had celebrated together, but the image itself offered a more [ambiguously|ambiguous|After “more”, use an adjective.] account. The curator resisted presenting the scene as simple evidence of unity.

title: The village meeting
text: The chairperson’s response was measured, even as the discussion grew [increasing|increasingly|Use the adverb “increasingly” before the adjective “heated”.] heated. She listened without interruption and answered each objection [dispassionately|dispassionate|Use an adverb to describe how she answered.] rather than dismissing it. Her calm manner [appeal|appealed|Use the past tense to match the meeting.] to residents who had expected a quarrel. Still, one resident’s account was [inadvertent|inadvertently|Use an adverb to describe how the detail was omitted.] left out of the minutes, changing how the decision appeared.

title: The gallery at closing time
text: At closing time, the gallery’s austere rooms seemed almost [luminously|luminous|After “seemed”, use an adjective.] beneath the low lamps. The fleeting reflection was [juxtaposing|juxtaposed|Use the past participle “juxtaposed” after “was” in this passive structure.] against the painted landscape. The guide’s final remark was [equivocal|equivocally|Use the adverb to modify “phrased”.] phrased, leaving the group unsure whether the artist had intended irony. One student [relinquish|relinquished|Use the past tense to match the completed action.] her seat to an older visitor before the doors closed.

title: A careful biography
text: The biography presented the scientist as benevolent, but it did not [reconciled|reconcile|Use the base form after “did not”.] every generous act with the private letters. Rather than treating the contradiction as a flaw, the author [juxtapose|juxtaposed|Use the past tense to match the rest of the paragraph.] the public speeches with quieter evidence. This method made the portrait more [credibly|credible|Use the adjective “credible” after “more”.] without pretending to resolve every uncertainty. The result was [disconcertingly|disconcerting|After “was”, use an adjective to describe the result.], yet the reader could see why the scientist remained admired.

title: The unfinished mural
text: The mural was meant to portray a triumphant voyage, but its final panel remained unfinished. A [despondently|despondent|Use an adjective after “a” to describe the expression.] expression on the sailor’s face complicated the celebratory tone. The painter [subtle|subtly|Use an adverb to describe how the painter altered the colours.] altered the colours near the horizon, making the scene less certain. Some viewers [interprets|interpreted|Use the past tense and plural subject “viewers”.] the change as regret; others saw only fatigue. The image [permeate|permeated|Use the past tense to match the discussion.] the gallery with a mood its title did not predict.

title: The disputed report
text: The report’s conclusion was [ostensible|ostensibly|Use the adverb “ostensibly” to modify “balanced”.] balanced, though its examples came almost entirely from one side. The author [reinforce|reinforced|Use the past tense to match the completed report.] that perspective by repeating the same claim in each section. title: The final interview
text: The interviewer’s questions were precise but not hostile, and the guest answered with [laconically|laconic|Use an adjective to describe the noun “restraint”.] restraint. A brief pause [insinuate|insinuated|Use the past tense to match the interview.] more than the following sentence stated outright. Viewers later disagreed about whether the silence conveyed grief or defiance.

title: The city garden
text: The city garden occupied a transient strip of land between two buildings, yet its popularity became [inexorably|inexorable|After “became”, use an adjective to describe the popularity.] once neighbours began meeting there. The organisers [prioritise|prioritised|Use the past tense to match the completed planning process.] shared tools and open access over decorative features when they planned the garden.
